The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It can be calculated as the product of the magnitudes of the vectors and the cosine of the angle between them. The dot product is also known as the scalar product and is denoted by the symbol "dot".

When two vectors are orthogonal, their dot product is zero. This is because the cosine of the angle between them is zero. In this case, the projection of one vector onto the other is zero, and the vectors are perpendicular to each other.

When a vector is projected onto another vector, the resulting vector is the component of the first vector that is parallel to the second vector. The magnitude of this component is the projection of the first vector onto the second vector, which is given by the formula |a|cos(theta), where a is the first vector and theta is the angle between them. The direction of the resulting vector is the same as the direction of the second vector.

Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
Return strict JSON with only root (element ID) and elements (object). Root element {"type":"Stack","props":{},"children":["leafId"]}. Each leaf has only type and props. Text props {text}; Metric {label,value}; Control {label,min,max,choices,value:{"$bindState":"/name"}}; Table {values:[{label,score}]}; Graphic {label,items}. Numeric inputs default to minima unless STATE supplies every binding. Read with {"$state":"/name"}. Computations use {"$computed":"Add","args":{"a":number,"b":number}}; Multiply and Excess have the same args, Excess means max(0,a-b). Rank takes args rows (array of [name,[three numeric scores]]), a,b,c (numeric weights) and produces sorted weighted rows. No other functions, properties or nesting of components.
